ITEM.PTXT: Load transfer during braking reduces the load on the rear wheels, causing the rear of the vehicle to lift. In anti-lift geometry, the geometric intersection point (OR) of the suspension is set higher than the ground contact surface. As a result, when the braking force (BR) acting on the rear wheels is supported at the intersection point (OR), component forces are generated toward the intersection point (BR1) and acting on the ground contact surface (BR2). Because the force acting on the ground contact surface is in the opposite direction to the tire reaction force against the sprung load reduced by braking, lift at the rear of the vehicle can be suppressed.
